features.title: Sessions
features.user_story: As a dashboard user, I want a multi-slot agent chat with one slot per conversation and pinned rows on top, so that I can run and return to several conversations at once.
features.entry_path: Rail → Sessions → new-chat button in ChatSidebar (or pick an existing row) → type in composer → Enter

preconditions.notes: Fake ACP backend must answer one turn so the transcript renders an assistant bubble. /chat/:slug? route in App.tsx; '/' and unknown paths redirect to /chat via ChatRedirect.

features.rationale: P0 core daily path (new session + send): open /chat, create or select a session, send, see the reply — four actions on the fake backend, no Electron or external account. Merged the feature-map 'Sessions' record with the code-derived new-session flow (same route, same flow).

features.title: Subagents
features.user_story: As a user, I want to see background agent runs spawned from a session with their status and a rail badge, so that I can follow delegated work.
features.entry_path: Chat activity viewer (right panel → Subagents); rail badge

preconditions.notes: Seed a spawn via POST /api/spawn against the fake backend.

features.rationale: P0: this is the subagent-run surface, and the newly merged collapsed subagent/nudge cards in the transcript are asserted here (seed a spawn via POST /api/spawn, check the collapsed card in the transcript, the Subagents tab and the rail badge). Spawn lifecycle is driven by the fake backend; render and stop are deterministic, but the seed step keeps it out of smoke.

features.title: Session title
features.user_story: As a user, I want auto-generated slot titles I can rename inline, so that sessions are recognisable in the sidebar.
features.entry_path: Header title → click to rename

preconditions.notes: Auto-generation path depends on the fake backend answering the title prompt.

features.rationale: Click, type, Enter — a daily micro-action with an immediate visible result.

features.title: Completed reply shows the muted elapsed-time footer
features.user_story: As a user, I want each finished reply to show how long it took, so that I can gauge responsiveness.
features.entry_path: Chat page > send message > completed reply footer

preconditions.notes: showTurnStats defaults on; fake ACP supplies no credits, so only elapsed renders.

features.rationale: Core chat path, three actions, deterministic on the fake backend.

features.title: Collapse the message input
features.user_story: As a reader, I want to put the composer away and restore it from a labelled bar showing my draft's first line, so that a long reply gets the whole pane.
features.entry_path: Composer + menu → Collapse the message input (touch: ⋯ overflow beside attach)

preconditions.notes: Preference persists in the browser; reset between runs.

features.rationale: Pure client toggle with persisted state; measurable layout change (89px) makes it a good pixel test.

features.title: Open an existing session via /chat/<slug> deep link
features.user_story: As a returning user, I want a bookmarked /chat/<key> URL to open that session, so that I can resume work directly.
features.entry_path: Direct navigation to /chat/<session-key> (also /orchestrated/<slug> redirects here)

preconditions.notes: Needs at least one persisted session key from the fixture; OrchestratedRedirect maps /orchestrated/:slug to /chat/:slug (assert the redirect in the same test).

features.rationale: Depends on fixture session keys and transcript rendering; fine on Xvfb+Chromium but not a smoke path since it needs seeded history. The /orchestrated redirect record was folded in because it lands on exactly this route.

features.title: Start an incognito/temporary session; it is badged and excluded from History and search
features.user_story: As a privacy-conscious user, I want incognito/temporary sessions labelled and kept out of history and memory surfaces, so that private chats leave no trace.
features.entry_path: ChatSidebar create menu > incognito/temporary session > send > sidebar row badge > History page > search

preconditions.notes: incognito-mix seeds three byte-identical transcripts differing only in memory_mode; memory_mode lives on the slot; startup video and artifact registration are skipped for restricted sessions.

features.rationale: Seed is built for exactly this assertion and all reads are local; the 'memory tools disabled' claim is not UI-observable on the fake backend, so the test asserts the badge and the History/search exclusion. Two incognito records merged.

features.title: Attach knowledge sources from the composer picker
features.user_story: As a user, I want to pick knowledge items to include in a turn, so that the agent answers from my documents.
features.entry_path: Composer > knowledge picker button > select item

preconditions.notes: KnowledgePicker.tsx + useKnowledgeFetch.ts; needs indexed knowledge items.

features.rationale: Requires knowledge fixture and embedding status; web-only.

features.title: Scroll a long transcript and load earlier messages
features.user_story: As a user with long sessions, I want earlier messages to load on demand, so that big transcripts stay responsive.
features.entry_path: Rail > Sessions > pinned long-history session > scroll to top > EarlierMessagesBar / Load earlier

preconditions.notes: Uses pages/chat/pagination.ts and EarlierMessagesBar; sessions-long-history initial load returns 8 live rows with has_more=true, next_before=60, and paging reads the archive segment.

features.rationale: Only this fixture makes the paging seam reachable through real routes; offline, but the heavy fixture and scroll timing keep it out of smoke. Two paging records merged.

features.title: Inspect MCP tools available to the session
features.user_story: As a user, I want to see which MCP tools the session can call, so that I understand the agent's capabilities.
features.entry_path: Chat footer > MCP info button > McpToolsPanel

preconditions.notes: McpInfoButton.tsx opens McpToolsPanel.tsx; McpOAuthBanner appears when a server needs sign-in.

features.rationale: Needs seeded MCP servers; OAuth completion is needs-secret and excluded from this record.

features.title: Pinned messages
features.user_story: As a user, I want to pin a message and see a per-session pins panel, so that key answers stay one click away.
features.entry_path: Message hover → pin; header pin count (or side panel → Pinned messages) opens the per-session pins panel

preconditions.notes: Session needs at least one assistant message. PinnedMessagesPanel.tsx; pins persist via api/pins.

features.rationale: Hover-revealed action plus a panel toggle and a persisted pin write; stable on the fake backend. Two records for the same pin flow merged.

features.title: Pinned prompt banner
features.user_story: As a reader of long replies, I want the turn's own prompt kept visible in a banner while I scroll, so that I never lose the question the answer belongs to.
features.entry_path: Settings → Chat → Pin the latest turn, then scroll a long reply in /chat

preconditions.notes: Needs a reply taller than the viewport.

features.rationale: Client-only geometry; needs a scroll-heavy fixture reply but is otherwise deterministic in Chromium.

features.title: Question cards
features.user_story: As a user, I want to answer an agent's multiple-choice question from a card in chat, so that decisions are one click.
features.entry_path: Inline PendingQuestionCard in the transcript

preconditions.notes: Seed a pending question via POST /api/ask-question.

features.rationale: Card can be seeded through the API without a live model; answer and dismissal are deterministic.

features.title: Regenerate / variants
features.user_story: As a user, I want to re-run a turn and switch between kept answers, so that I can compare responses.
features.entry_path: Message action → Regenerate; variant switcher on the bubble

preconditions.notes: Fake ACP backend should return distinct text per regenerate to make variants visible.

features.rationale: Requires the fake backend to produce a second answer; fine on the nightly harness.

features.title: Rewind
features.user_story: As a user, I want to drop the transcript back to an earlier turn, so that I can redo the conversation from that point.
features.entry_path: Message action → Rewind

preconditions.notes: Session with ≥3 turns.

features.rationale: Deterministic transcript mutation on a fixture session; visually verifiable by turn count.

features.title: Session summary
features.user_story: As a user, I want a rolling summary of the conversation in the right panel, so that I can catch up on a long session at a glance.
features.entry_path: Chat right panel → Summary tab

preconditions.notes: Summary generation runs through the fake backend.

features.rationale: Panel tab plus one backend call; not a top-five path.

features.title: Share message as card
features.user_story: As a user, I want to turn an assistant reply into a branded PNG card with a prefilled caption, so that I can post it to X or LinkedIn.
features.entry_path: Message hover → More actions → Share as image

preconditions.notes: social_share_enabled must be true in /api/dashboard/config (shareSupport.ts); a policy pin withdraws the entry. External posting is out of scope.

features.rationale: Card rendering is client-side canvas in Chromium and the governance probe is a config read, so fixtures suffice; the actual X/LinkedIn post is not asserted (no network). Two share records merged.

features.title: Side chat
features.user_story: As a user, I want a scratch sub-conversation beside the main turn, opened from the panel, /side, or 'Ask about this' on selected text, so that I can ask a tangent without polluting the main transcript.
features.entry_path: Chat right panel → Side; or /side in the composer; or select assistant text → Ask about this

preconditions.notes: Text selection toolbar needs a rendered assistant message. Side turn runs an isolated LLM session against the fake ACP, which returns the canned reply; closing drops the buffer (main transcript untouched).

features.rationale: Three entry points (panel tab, /side, Ask about this) into one sub-turn served by the fake backend offline; assert the side reply and the untouched main transcript. Three overlapping side-chat records merged; four actions via any one door.

features.title: Tool approvals
features.user_story: As a user, I want to approve or deny a tool call the agent proposes from an inline card, so that risky actions never run without me.
features.entry_path: Inline ApprovalCard in the transcript during a turn

preconditions.notes: Fake ACP backend must emit a permission request; if it has no such sentinel (only [[SLOW]]/[[ERROR]] are documented), seed the approval via the gateway API or add a sentinel before this can run.

features.rationale: Requires the fake backend (or an API seed) to raise an approval; then a single click and visible resolution. Nightly because the trigger is a harness dependency, not a user action.

features.title: Turn minimap
features.user_story: As a desktop user reading a long transcript, I want a proportional marker rail in the left gutter with hover previews and click/arrow-key jumps, so that I can navigate turns quickly.
features.entry_path: Session transcript → left gutter (viewport ≥768px, pane ≥560px, ≥2 turns, fine pointer)

preconditions.notes: Set viewport to at least 1280x900 and a non-coarse pointer; two or more turns required. TurnNavigationMinimap.tsx.

features.rationale: Visible only under viewport and pointer conditions the harness can set; hover previews and click/arrow-key jumps are testable on Xvfb. Feature-map and code-derived minimap records merged; three actions (open long session, hover a marker, click it).

features.title: Worktrees
features.user_story: As a developer, I want to create a git worktree for a follow-up session from a card, so that parallel work stays isolated.
features.entry_path: Chat follow-up card → Start in new worktree

preconditions.notes: Project directory must be a git repository; the follow-up card must be seeded (suggest_followup via API), since the fake backend does not call MCP tools.

features.rationale: Needs a git repo fixture and an API-seeded follow-up card; creating a worktree is local and reversible.

features.title: Send a second side-chat question while one streams and see it steered or queued
features.user_story: As a user, I want a second question during a streaming side turn to be steered in or shown as a queue card, so that nothing I typed is dropped.
features.entry_path: Chat page > Side Chat tab > send [[SLOW]] > send again

preconditions.notes: [[SLOW]] makes the fake stream chunks with delay; busy-send mode is per-slot (mc-busy-send-mode:<slot>). Queue cards support cancel/edit, server-confirmed.

features.rationale: Deterministic via the fake backend's SLOW sentinel; steer/queue cards render in the panel.

features.title: An MCP App renders inline in chat as a sandboxed iframe with a live bridge
features.user_story: As a user, I want interactive app UI from an MCP server to render in the transcript, so that I can act on it without leaving chat.
features.entry_path: Chat page > agent tool result carrying an app render marker

preconditions.notes: Requires gatewayd and an MCP server that returns SEP-1865 UI; the fake ACP emits only canned tool cards.

features.rationale: Not reachable on the fake backend/no-network target.

features.title: Complete MCP OAuth from the chat banner
features.user_story: As a user, I want to sign in to an MCP server when prompted in chat, so that its tools become available.
features.entry_path: Chat > McpOAuthBanner > Sign in > provider OAuth > return

preconditions.notes: McpRowSignIn on Connections tab is the other door.

features.rationale: Requires a real OAuth provider account.

features.title: workflow_run shows a launch card and later a completion card in chat
features.user_story: As a user, I want visible cards when a workflow starts and finishes, so that I can follow it from the transcript.
features.entry_path: Chat page > ask for a dynamic workflow

preconditions.notes: Needs a model that calls the kirocrew-core workflow_run MCP tool; the fake backend cannot.

features.rationale: Depends on real MCP tool execution by a model, absent on the fake ACP target.

features.title: Source-provider review
features.user_story: As a developer, I want PR state, checks and review threads in the Changes panel, so that I can review without leaving the chat.
features.entry_path: Chat right panel → Changes

preconditions.notes: Needs a GitHub or GitLab token and a linked PR URL in the transcript.

features.rationale: Fetching PR state requires a real source-provider token.

features.title: Toggle the Activity side panel from the session header
features.user_story: As a user, I want to open the Activity panel beside the transcript, so that I can watch tool calls and subagents while chatting.
features.entry_path: Session header > activity panel toggle (or Ctrl/Cmd chord dispatching 'toggle-activity-panel')

preconditions.notes: Panel portals into #activity-bar-slot on desktop; dock position from useSidePanelDock (right or bottom). PINNED_VIEWS = changes, artifacts, files are always present and non-closable, even when empty.

features.rationale: Three actions, pure web layout: open a session, toggle the side panel, assert the pinned Changes/Artifacts/Files tabs. High-value regression surface for the shell grid; two overlapping side-panel records merged.

features.title: App-contributed chat surfaces (panel tabs, session controls)
features.user_story: As a user of an installed app, I want its declared side-panel tabs in the chat + menu and its sessionControls chip in the composer bar, so that app UI sits beside my conversation.
features.entry_path: Chat right panel > + menu > the app's row (launcher card on an empty panel); composer bar chip when an enabled app declares contributes.sessionControls

preconditions.notes: At least one enabled fixture app declaring contributes.panelTabs (bundled ESM tab) and contributes.sessionControls with a status route.

features.rationale: Both surfaces mount deterministically from the manifest plus a status GET once the apps-installed fixture bundles the ESM tab; merged because both are the same flow (app contribution appears in chat) on the same route.

features.title: Ctrl+G opens the Subagents activity tab on the chat page
features.user_story: As a user following a crew pipeline, I want Ctrl+G to jump to the Subagents tab, so that the kiro-cli hint 'Press ctrl+g to monitor progress' works.
features.entry_path: Any page > Ctrl+G

preconditions.notes: Literal Ctrl on every platform, routes to /chat.

features.rationale: Keyboard chord to a client-side route; no backend needed.

features.title: Open Issues, Links, Subagents, Workflows, Logs, Context, Git, Summary and Pins views from the + menu
features.user_story: As a user, I want to add on-demand views to the side panel, so that I can inspect logs, links or a session summary when I need them.
features.entry_path: Chat page > side panel + menu

preconditions.notes: Transcript-fed views (issues, links, pins) render honest empty states on fixture sessions with no URLs.

features.rationale: All views are singleton SPA tabs whose data comes from the slot or transcript already loaded; no Electron or network.

features.title: Terminal panel
features.user_story: As a developer, I want a docked PTY and a per-chat terminal opening on the chat's working directory, so that I can run commands beside the conversation.
features.entry_path: Header terminal toggle (docked); right panel → + → Terminal (per-chat)

preconditions.notes: Gateway host must allow PTY spawn; run a harmless echo.

features.rationale: PTY over WebSocket works in plain Chromium against the gateway; not native-only.

features.title: Open a docked terminal tab and run a command
features.user_story: As a developer, I want a terminal beside the chat, so that I can run commands in the session's project directory.
features.entry_path: Chat page → side panel + menu → Terminal

preconditions.notes: Linux PTY is supported; keep commands to `echo`.

features.rationale: PTY works on Linux/Xvfb and the xterm output is visible; not smoke because it spawns a shell.

features.title: Terminal rail row toggles the docked terminal panel
features.user_story: As a user, I want a terminal docked in the dashboard, so that I can run commands next to the agent.
features.entry_path: Rail bottom section > Terminal row (aria-pressed) > BottomTerminalPanel opens

preconditions.notes: Hidden when /api/terminal/sessions returns enabled:false; panel position from useTerminalPosition.

features.rationale: Needs a backend PTY endpoint; xterm renders headless but a real shell process may be unavailable in CI.

features.title: Sidebar groups sessions under the Demos folder and History shows the closed Research notes session
features.user_story: As a returning user, I want folders, pinned sessions and a History panel, so that I can find past work quickly.
features.entry_path: Sidebar sessions list > Demos folder > History panel

preconditions.notes: 3 active slots (starter pinned, coder-demo, triage-demo in Demos) plus closed research-notes and an archive slice.

features.rationale: P0: this is the newly merged list-shell sidebar (folders, pinned rows, History pane) rendered read-only on the rich seed in ≤5 actions; the seed is designed for it.

features.title: Older sessions
features.user_story: As a user, I want a searchable history pane of closed sessions with per-session and bulk delete, so that I can revisit or prune past work.
features.entry_path: Sidebar → Older Sessions disclosure

preconditions.notes: Only exercise open, search and single delete; skip Delete all on shared fixtures.

features.rationale: Open disclosure, search, open a session — a core retrieval path; the bulk delete is destructive and left out of the smoke script.

features.title: Sessions page
features.user_story: As a dashboard user, I want a bookmarkable session chooser with search, filter chips and recency groups, so that I can pick a session without one being auto-selected or auto-created.
features.entry_path: Type or bookmark /sessions (no rail row) > search / filter chip > click a row > opens /chat/<key>

preconditions.notes: At least one tagged and one unread session to exercise the chips. Lazy-loaded SessionsPage.

features.rationale: Read-only list at a stable URL; open, search, click a chip or row — trivially pixel-testable. Moved the code-derived chooser record from the chat bucket (it is a session list, not a transcript) and merged it.

features.title: Collapse and expand the left nav rail
features.user_story: As a user, I want to collapse the rail to icons, so that I have more room for content.
features.entry_path: Rail header brand button (title 'Collapse sidebar') > click > hover collapsed icon shows portal tooltip

preconditions.notes: Persists to localStorage 'mc-nav'; collapsed rows show flyout label via useNavTip.

features.rationale: Two clicks, pure shell chrome, high regression value.

features.title: Rail shows Main group in registry order with one active row
features.user_story: As a user, I want the rail to list Sessions, Schedule, Artifacts, then Apps/Discover/Library, then Agent Capabilities and Settings, so that navigation is predictable.
features.entry_path: Load any page > inspect rail rows and active highlight

preconditions.notes: Order = builtins.tsx registration order filtered by group; Notifications, Webhooks, Explore are hiddenFromNav; Members hidden unless mc-preview-crew=1.

features.rationale: Single-load visual assertion covering the surface registry; the cheapest guard against rail regressions.

features.title: Fork a session
features.user_story: As a user, I want to branch a new slot from an existing transcript, keeping incognito or temporary mode on the child, so that I can explore an alternative without losing the original.
features.entry_path: Session row menu → Fork

preconditions.notes: Cover one persistent and one incognito parent to check mode inheritance.

features.rationale: Single POST with a visible new sidebar row; the mode-inheritance branch needs the incognito seed.

features.title: Session folders
features.user_story: As a user with many sessions, I want to group session rows into folders and start mode-pinned ephemeral chats inside them, so that my sidebar stays organised.
features.entry_path: Sidebar folder header → drag a row; folder ⋯ menu → New ephemeral chat

preconditions.notes: Drag-and-drop requires pointer events; fixture should include one existing folder.

features.rationale: Folder create plus drag interaction is reproducible in Chromium but is more than a smoke path. Kept separate from the read-only list-shell smoke (sidebar-folders-history-and-archive) because this one exercises organising, not rendering.

features.title: Session tags
features.user_story: As a user, I want to put coloured labels on sessions and filter by them, so that I can find related conversations quickly.
features.entry_path: Sidebar row context menu → Tags

preconditions.notes: Fixture seeds at least one tag via /api/chat/tags.

features.rationale: Context menu plus tag picker plus filter is deterministic UI; not a top-five daily path.

features.title: Drag to reorder app rows in the rail
features.user_story: As a user, I want to reorder my app shortcuts, so that my most-used apps are on top.
features.entry_path: Rail > Apps rows > mouse drag one row over another (dnd-kit, 8px threshold)

preconditions.notes: Persists to APP_NAV_ORDER_KEY; hidden (unpinned) apps keep their slot via buildReorderBaseline.

features.rationale: Pointer drag needs real mouse events; works in headless Chromium but flaky enough to keep out of smoke.

features.title: Apps list collapses behind an 'N more' toggle
features.user_story: As a user with many apps, I want the Apps section to fold past six rows, so that the rail stays compact.
features.entry_path: Rail > Apps section > 'N more' NavToggle > 'Show less'

preconditions.notes: APPS_NAV_LIMIT = 6; state persisted in 'mc-apps-expanded'; needs more than 6 enabled apps with UI pages.

features.rationale: Needs the apps-installed fixture to exceed the limit; web-only.

features.title: Focus mode hides chrome and reveals it on edge hover
features.user_story: As a user, I want focus mode to hide the header and rail, so that the active surface fills the window.
features.entry_path: Topbar focus-mode-toggle button > move pointer to top/left edge strips (focus-peek-top / focus-peek-rail)

preconditions.notes: Desktop only; body classes mc-focus-mode/mc-focus-chrome; Electron traffic-light handling is skipped in web.

features.rationale: Hover-intent timers make it a nightly rather than smoke case; degrades cleanly without Electron.

features.title: Open the mobile nav drawer via hamburger and swipe
features.user_story: As a phone user, I want a drawer for navigation, so that the rail does not consume the screen.
features.entry_path: Viewport <768px > topbar hamburger (MobileNavGlyph) or edge swipe > drawer > tap row closes

preconditions.notes: useIsMobile breakpoint; drawer animated by animateDrawer; Escape and scrim close it.

features.rationale: Requires a narrow viewport emulation and touch events; web-only.

features.title: Report issue from the rail opens the diagnostics modal
features.user_story: As a user hitting a bug, I want to report it with logs attached, so that triage has evidence.
features.entry_path: Rail community row > 'Report issue' button > ReportProblemModal

preconditions.notes: Also reachable from Settings > About > Support; final step opens a pre-filled GitHub issue.

features.rationale: Modal renders headless; the GitHub hand-off is external and not asserted.

features.title: Pinned, open, closed-in-History and archived sessions render in their respective places
features.user_story: As a user, I want each session state to appear where I expect (slots, History, archive), so that nothing looks lost.
features.entry_path: Sidebar > Sessions page and History

preconditions.notes: Four sessions cover the four states.

features.rationale: Seeded transcript JSONL is the whole input; offline.

features.title: Switch between default, review and research workspaces and see distinct memory and pinned sessions
features.user_story: As a user with several projects, I want to switch workspace, so that memory and sessions scoped to it are what I see.
features.entry_path: Sidebar > workspace switcher

preconditions.notes: One session per workspace selects a different agent; agent identity is per session.

features.rationale: Config-driven UI with seeded differences; offline.

features.title: Open the Connect your phone dialog
features.user_story: As a user, I want to pair my phone, so that I can use the dashboard on mobile.
features.entry_path: Rail bottom > 'Connect your phone' row > MobileConnectModal

preconditions.notes: Row only appears when /api/mobile-connect methods returns a renderable kind; closes on any navigation.

features.rationale: Kept needs-secret: the row only appears when /api/mobile-connect returns a renderable method, and every real method (tunnel/tailnet) needs an external account the no-network target lacks. Rendering the modal against a stubbed method would be a nightly degraded check.

features.title: Promote a capability tab to the rail
features.user_story: As a daily user of one capability tab, I want to pin it as its own rail row (up to NAV_PINNED_LIMIT), so that it is one click away instead of two.
features.entry_path: Agent Capabilities page header → pin control (PinSurfaceButton) on the current tab

preconditions.notes: Preference is browser-local under mc-nav-pinned (useNavPinned); clear between runs. CAPABILITY_SUB_ITEMS registered pinnable; promotedTabOwner logic in App.tsx yields active state on the host row.

features.rationale: Client-only preference with an immediate rail change; easy to pixel-assert. Two pin-to-rail records merged.

features.title: Redirect /agents and /mc-agents
features.user_story: As a user with an old bookmark, I want /agents and /mc-agents to land on Agent Capabilities, so that deep links keep working.
features.entry_path: Type /agents or /mc-agents → /capabilities
features.rationale: Navigation-only assertion.

features.title: Redirect /artifacts/deploy
features.user_story: As a user with an old bookmark, I want /artifacts/deploy to land on /deploy, so that deep links keep working.
features.entry_path: Type /artifacts/deploy → /deploy
features.rationale: Navigation-only assertion.

features.title: Redirect /connections
features.user_story: As a user with an old bookmark, I want /connections to land on the Connections tab, so that deep links keep working.
features.entry_path: Type /connections → /capabilities?tab=mcp
features.rationale: Navigation-only assertion.

features.title: Redirect /instances
features.user_story: As a user with an old bookmark, I want /instances to land on Settings Instances, so that deep links keep working.
features.entry_path: Type /instances → /settings/instances
features.rationale: Navigation-only assertion.

features.title: Redirect /knowledge
features.user_story: As a user with an old bookmark, I want /knowledge to land on the Knowledge tab, so that deep links keep working.
features.entry_path: Type /knowledge → lands on /capabilities?tab=knowledge
features.rationale: One navigation and a URL assertion.

features.title: Redirect /overview
features.user_story: As a user with an old bookmark, I want /overview to land on Settings Overview, so that deep links keep working.
features.entry_path: Type /overview → /settings/overview
features.rationale: Navigation-only assertion.

features.title: Redirect /tasks
features.user_story: As a user with an old bookmark, I want /tasks to land on Task Runner, so that deep links keep working.
features.entry_path: Type /tasks → /projects
features.rationale: Navigation-only assertion.

features.title: Redirect unmatched paths
features.user_story: As a user who mistypes a URL, I want anything unmatched to land on /chat, so that I am never stranded.
features.entry_path: Type any unknown path → /chat
features.rationale: Navigation-only assertion.

features.title: Legacy ?tab= query URL redirects to canonical path
features.user_story: As a user following an old bookmark, I want /settings?tab=channels&channel=slack to land on /settings/channels/slack, so that saved links keep working.
features.entry_path: Navigate directly to a legacy query-param settings URL; page replaces it with the path form

preconditions.notes: Test must navigate via address bar to the legacy form; start_url itself has no query string per schema.

features.rationale: Regression check on URL translation; not a daily path but fully web-testable.

features.title: Update available shows pill, Settings dot, and update overlay
features.user_story: As a user, I want clear update progress, so that I know when the gateway is restarting.
features.entry_path: Fixture status update_available=true > UpdatePill in topbar + dot on Settings row > Update Now > UpdateOverlay steps

preconditions.notes: UpdateOverlay exported for capture harness; real apply restarts the gateway.

features.rationale: Re-tiered excluded -> nightly: with the fake backend returning status update_available=true the UpdatePill, About-tab dot and UpdateOverlay all render offline in Chromium. The test stops at the overlay and never clicks apply (which would restart the gateway and kill the session).

features.title: Request a feature from the topbar feedback pill
features.user_story: As a user, I want a one-click feature request, so that the agent files it for me.
features.entry_path: Topbar FeedbackPill > Request a Feature > new session created with seeded prompt

preconditions.notes: requestFeature() creates a slot, seeds hidden context, sends canned message via sendTurn; error row on refused send.

features.rationale: Creates a session against the fake backend; web-only.

features.title: Browser panel

features.title: Files: open a folder, browse the tree, and read a file
features.user_story: As a user, I want to open a directory on the gateway host and read a file in a tab, so that I can inspect files without leaving the dashboard.
features.entry_path: Enable Files > Rail > Files > path bar > open folder > click file in tree

preconditions.notes: Read-only backend on an auto port proxied at /apps/file-explorer/api; reachable paths limited to home, /tmp, /opt. git/ripgrep optional.

features.rationale: Fully local and read-only; separate backend process and filesystem fixture make it a nightly check rather than smoke.

features.title: Notes: enable the app, attach a local vault and edit a note
features.user_story: As a writer, I want to attach an existing markdown folder as a vault and edit a note in place, so that my notes stay versioned and portable beside the agent.
features.entry_path: Apps > Library > Notes > Enable > Rail > Notes (/md-notebook) > Connect vault > Attach existing folder > open note > click block to edit

preconditions.notes: Attach-folder path needs no credentials; use a scratch git repo created by the lane. Backend is a managed subprocess on an auto port proxied at /apps/md-notebook/api. Cloning a private repo or sync needs a PAT/gh and a remote and is not asserted.

features.rationale: Local folder attach + in-place edit is fully offline and headless-capable, spawning only the app backend and git on a local tree; git clone/push variants would be needs-secret.

features.title: Personal Shopper: save preferences and start an advisor conversation
features.user_story: As a shopper, I want to save my preferences and start a conversation with the advisor agent, so that I get store research without it ever buying anything.
features.entry_path: Enable Personal Shopper > Rail > Personal Shopper > Preferences tab > add preference > Start conversation

preconditions.notes: Start conversation creates a chat slot pinned to the personal-shopper-advisor agent and navigates to chat. Store research needs outbound web access by the agent and is not asserted; the page itself does not.

features.rationale: Kept nightly rather than needs-secret: the asserted flow ends at preferences CRUD and slot creation, which are fixture-backed and run against the fake ACP backend; real product research would need network and is explicitly outside the flow.

features.title: Create Folders From Project: scan a project and create sidebar folders
features.user_story: As a developer with a monorepo, I want to scan a project directory and tick sub-projects, so that matching sidebar folders are created without duplicates.
features.entry_path: Enable Create Folders From Project > Rail > Create Folders > pick project root > Scan > tick rows > Create

preconditions.notes: Scan is read-only via /api/project-scaffold; needs a project directory with detectable sub-packages on disk. Uses the shared ProjectPicker (recent + browse).

features.rationale: Fully local, native-control UI; needs a fixture project tree on disk, so nightly rather than smoke.

features.title: Spec Builder: pick a project, generate requirements, and approve
features.user_story: As an engineer, I want to turn a feature idea into Requirements -> Design -> Tasks with an embedded agent and approve each stage, so that an execution session builds the approved plan.
features.entry_path: Enable Spec Builder > Rail > Spec Builder > New spec > choose project folder and mode > chat idea > review docs card > Approve

preconditions.notes: Embeds ChatEmbed scoped to /api/chat; optional fresh worktree creation touches git in the chosen project. Generated markdown comes from the agent over the ACP backend.

features.rationale: Local project + embedded chat run headless with a fake backend that returns markdown; multi-stage approval flow is too long for smoke.

features.title: Workflows: load an example script, validate it, and run it
features.user_story: As an orchestrator, I want to validate a dynamic-workflow script and run it, so that I watch phases and agent events stream without arbitrary Python executing.
features.entry_path: Enable workflows (hidden app; CLI or fixture) > Rail > Workflows > Author tab > load example > Validate > Run > Runs tab

preconditions.notes: Hidden from the App Store grid; enable via `kirocrew app enable workflows` or the fixture. Backend on auto port proxied at /apps/workflows/api; synchronous /run returns the full event stream. Agent calls go through the ACP backend.

features.rationale: Shipped examples and a sandboxed validator make it deterministic headless with the fake backend; hidden-app enable and separate backend process keep it out of smoke.

features.title: App detail
features.user_story: As a user, I want one app's manifest, config, permissions and uninstall in one page, so that I can audit and manage it.

preconditions.notes: Do not press uninstall on shared fixtures.

features.rationale: Read-only manifest and config render; uninstall is destructive and excluded from the script. Kept separate from Discover because the flow is the audit view, not browse/enable.

features.title: Installed app page
features.user_story: As a user, I want an app's own UI served inside the dashboard and builtin apps to claim their own top-level routes, so that I use them without leaving.
features.entry_path: Rail > Apps rows > click app > /apps/<name> (AppPage iframe/ESM) or builtin /<app>/* resolved through the /:builtinApp catch-all (BuiltinAppRoute)

preconditions.notes: Fixture app ships a static UI. Sample two or three builtin routes (e.g. /worlds, /channels). Installed apps do not highlight Discover or Library; orphaned apps tint warn.

features.rationale: Token mint and iframe/ESM mount are deterministic with a fixture app; builtin route resolution is deterministic and individual app content is owned per app.

features.title: Updates
features.user_story: As a user, I want to see installed apps with a newer version and update them, so that I stay current.
features.entry_path: Rail > Discover (updates badge) > Updates sub-tab (/apps/-/updates)

preconditions.notes: Fixture pins an installed version older than the stubbed registry; countUpdatables compares registry rows to installed and the badge is merged via discoverBadges only.

features.rationale: Depends on a version delta between the fixture and a stubbed registry; web-only and deterministic once that fixture exists.

features.title: Auto-Improvement: connect a GitHub repo, calibrate ruler, view findings
features.user_story: As a maintainer, I want to connect a GitHub repository, calibrate a performance ruler, and review findings drafted as PRs, so that only measured wins reach review.
features.entry_path: Enable Auto-Improvement > Rail > Auto-Improve > Setup panel > connect repo and base branch > calibrate ruler

preconditions.notes: Requires git and an authenticated `gh` CLI on the gateway host plus a real GitHub repository; drafts pull requests via /api/source/pull-request.

features.rationale: Primary flow depends on an authenticated gh CLI and a real GitHub repo to clone, measure, and draft PRs against; the empty setup panel alone could be checked nightly but is not the primary flow.

features.title: AWS Control: view account health and browse the S3 cloud drive
features.user_story: As an operator, I want to see my AWS accounts with health lights and browse my S3-backed cloud drive, so that I can manage files and backups from the dashboard.
features.entry_path: Enable AWS Control > Rail > AWS Control > Files rail section; Accounts & credentials at rail foot

preconditions.notes: Needs real AWS credentials/profiles on the gateway host; bucket creation is gated behind a paid-service consent card. No target fixture provides AWS connections.

features.rationale: Every meaningful surface (account health, drive listing, share links) requires live AWS credentials and an S3 bucket the user owns; the target has no network and no credentials.

features.title: Code Review Sage: add a repo and review a pull request
features.user_story: As a reviewer, I want to add a GitHub repository and run a deep review of a pull request, so that I get a prioritized Focus Report before reading the diff myself.
features.entry_path: Enable Code Review Sage > Rail > Code Review Sage > Add repos > pick PR > Review

preconditions.notes: Requires an authenticated `gh` CLI on the gateway host and a real GitHub repository with open pull requests.

features.rationale: Repository discovery, PR listing, and draft review staging all go through the authenticated gh CLI against GitHub.

features.title: Crew Companion: set break interval and add a reminder
features.user_story: As a desktop user, I want to configure break nudges and add a plain-language reminder, so that the floating companion paces my day.
features.entry_path: Kiro Crew Desktop > enable Crew Companion > Rail > Crew Companion > Settings section > Reminders section

preconditions.notes: platform.requiresDesktopApp=true; the companion runs as a separate desktop process on 127.0.0.1:7778 proxied via /apps/crew-companion/api. In a browser the page shows a 'not running' state.

features.rationale: Requires the Electron desktop app and its companion process; the target has no Electron. Degradable to web-only only for the offline landing state and cached Memories.

features.title: Issue Radar: connect a repository and triage issues
features.user_story: As a maintainer, I want to connect a GitHub/GitLab/Azure repo and triage issues with AI-suggested labels, so that nothing is re-investigated.
features.entry_path: Enable Issue Radar > Rail > Issue Radar > Welcome carousel > Connect repository > pick issue > investigate

preconditions.notes: Needs an authenticated provider CLI (gh, glab, or az) on the gateway host and a real repository. WelcomeCarousel renders with no repos connected.

features.rationale: Repository connection, issue caching, and every write go through authenticated provider CLIs; only the welcome carousel is reachable without them.

features.title: Meetings: start a meeting and capture live transcript with notes
features.user_story: As an attendee, I want to start a meeting and have it transcribed with notes and action items, so that I can review tasks before filing them.
features.entry_path: Enable Meetings > Rail > Meetings > New/upcoming meeting > Start > allow microphone > End > Task review

preconditions.notes: Needs browser microphone permission and Kiro Crew's speech-to-text over /api/ws/stt (STT backend dependencies like faster-whisper are optional heavy installs not present in the target image). Calendar via optional .ics path; agents via ACP backend.

features.rationale: The primary flow needs a working STT backend (an optional heavy install the no-network target cannot fetch) and a calendar/audio source; only the empty meeting list and settings views render from fixtures, and that is not the primary flow.

features.title: Mochi: enable the desktop pet and view activity, watchlist, and plan
features.user_story: As a desktop user, I want a pet that floats on my screen and watches pages for me, so that I am tapped only when something changed.
features.entry_path: Kiro Crew Desktop > enable Mochi > Rail > Mochi > status row > Activity / Watchlist / Plan tabs

preconditions.notes: platform.requiresDesktopApp=true; pet/panel/settings windows are Electron HTML windows. Dashboard page shows an offline landing with Enable CTA when disabled.

features.rationale: Pet window, click-through transparency, and panel windows need Electron, which the target lacks; the dashboard data page alone is degradable to web-only.

features.title: Ops Mission Control: configure a provider and work an incident on the board
features.user_story: As an on-call engineer, I want alarms claimed and investigated automatically, so that the second occurrence resolves faster than the first.
features.entry_path: Enable Ops Mission Control > Rail > Mission Control > Settings tab > add provider > Board tab > open incident chat

preconditions.notes: Providers are AWS CloudWatch, PagerDuty, Datadog, GitHub Issues, or a signed-webhook POST. App ships crons (dispatch, reconcile, rotation-check, ledger-hygiene). Slack output reuses an existing Slack connection.

features.rationale: Primary flow needs a real monitoring provider credential; a signed generic webhook could degrade this to nightly but the board is empty without a configured provider.

features.title: Papyrus: create a paper, edit LaTeX, and compile to PDF
features.user_story: As an author, I want to write LaTeX beside a live PDF preview and compile on save, so that errors jump to the offending line.
features.entry_path: Enable Papyrus > Rail > Papyrus > New paper > edit source > Cmd/Ctrl+S to compile > view PDF

preconditions.notes: Compile needs tectonic or pdflatex preinstalled on PATH in the nightly image (the one-click managed Tectonic install needs network and is unavailable). Clone/push needs non-interactive git credentials and is out of scope.

features.rationale: Excluded: compiling to PDF needs a TeX toolchain the lane's runner image does not install, so the asserted end state is unreachable; a create-and-edit-only scenario without compile could be nightly. Paper creation and editing are local; compile needs a TeX toolchain preinstalled in the nightly image, and git remote flows would be needs-secret.

features.title: PPTX Maker: open the studio, browse the library, and start a deck chat
features.user_story: As a presenter, I want to describe a deck in chat and watch slides appear in a live preview, so that I get a real .pptx without a design tool.
features.entry_path: Enable PPTX Maker > Rail > PPTX Maker > Decks view > New deck (choose Spec/Vibe agent) > chat > watch preview

preconditions.notes: First use installs the sha256-pinned spec-driven-presentation-maker engine from the network; @sdpm MCP tools and optional soffice/pdftoppm needed for full previews. Generation happens in a chat session on a shipped agent.

features.rationale: The primary flow (start a deck chat, watch preview) requires the engine download and MCP tools that need network, which the target does not have; the Decks/Library/Settings views render headless but are not the primary flow.

features.title: App migration
features.user_story: As a user, I want to move an app's data after a packaging change, so that nothing is lost on upgrade.
features.entry_path: Rail > orphaned app (warn icon) or Apps > migration prompt (/apps/migrate/:name); MigrationCheck banner in <main>

preconditions.notes: Fixture app flagged as orphaned/needing migration; MigrationCheck is mounted route-independently. Cleanup DELETE is destructive and runs only on a throwaway copy.

features.rationale: Excluded until a fixture ships an orphaned app: no tests_fixtures seed carries one, so the migration page (/apps/migrate/<name>) is unreachable on the target. Page renders from fixture state and mutates only fixture state; needs an orphaned-app fixture.

features.title: Task Runner
features.user_story: As a user, I want autonomous multi-step runs from a spec -- compose, refine, plan, run, then follow one run's steps, gates and approvals -- so that large tasks proceed without babysitting.
features.entry_path: Rail (Apps group) > Task Runner (/projects; /tasks redirects) > Compose tab > describe work > Plan > Run > project row /projects/<id> (DAG/Phased views, TaskDetailPanel, approve gate)

preconditions.notes: defaultEnabled=true; surface 'projects' is appOnly and served by BuiltinAppRoute. Fake ACP backend answers the plan and refinement-question calls; seed one project with activities and a pending gate for the detail/approval assertions. Badge is the task-gate approval count via appBadges. Spec and YAML modes are alternative entry tabs.

features.rationale: Enabled by default and a core autonomy path: open page, type description, Plan, Run, observe progress -- five actions against the fake ACP backend; listing projects and the detail/gate view are fixture-driven. Planning talks to the ACP backend, which the target provides as the fake backend.

features.title: Agent Worlds: open the 3D scene page, switch scene, pop out
features.user_story: As a user running several agents, I want an ambient 3D scene of my crew with switchable themes, so that I can see at a glance how busy Kiro Crew is.
features.entry_path: Enable Agent Worlds in App Store > Rail > Worlds (/worlds via BuiltinAppRoute) > scene picker (office, ghost, panda, underwater, wizard tower, watering hole, neural constellation, mission control) > popout

preconditions.notes: App is defaultEnabled=false; enable via App Store or fixture. WebGL via three.js; scene choice persists in localStorage; pop-out uses window.open (WorldsPopout.tsx).

features.rationale: Pure visualization over the live agent list, no external service. WebGL renders under SwiftShader in headless Chromium but pixels are nondeterministic; assert canvas presence and picker state only.

features.title: Manage worktrees and pods on the Dev Fleet page
features.user_story: As a developer, I want to see worktrees and agent pods, so that I can coordinate parallel work.
features.entry_path: Builtin app route /dev-fleet (BuiltinAppRoute) → worktree list → pod system

preconditions.notes: DevFleetPage.tsx with devFleetApi.ts; creates/removes git worktrees. Read-only listing only.

features.rationale: The page itself renders from fixture state and is the observable flow; starting a pod needs a container runtime the target lacks, so pod lifecycle stays out of the scenario. Read-only listing is safe on fixture repos; worktree deletion should not be exercised. Local git only, no network.

features.title: Schedule
features.user_story: As a user, I want to see my scheduled jobs with status and next run and create new cron jobs (agent turns, scripts, commands), so that routine work runs on time.
features.entry_path: Rail → Schedule → list (two active, one paused with expressions) → Add job → save; also crew editor → What wakes this crew

preconditions.notes: Gateway runs with --no-crons, so jobs never fire; seed provides three deterministic rows. Creating a job writes to the throwaway home only.

features.rationale: Listing and adding a job is THE core daily path of the bucket and stays under five actions; seeded rows make the list assertion deterministic and the create writes only to the throwaway home.

features.title: Switch Schedule between list, calendar, and executions views
features.user_story: As a user with cron jobs, I want list, calendar, and execution-history views, so that I can see when jobs run and what happened.
features.entry_path: Rail → Schedule → view segmented control (list | calendar | executions)

preconditions.notes: Sorting via useSortableTable.

features.rationale: Core daily surface; three clicks; fixture provides jobs and executions.

features.title: Cron secret grants
features.user_story: As an owner, I want to approve, deny or revoke vault-secret env grants a script cron requested, so that scripts get secrets only with my consent.
features.entry_path: Schedule → script job → drawer → Secrets section → approve

preconditions.notes: Seed a script job with a pending secret request and a vault secret it names. Unit-covered by SchedulePage.secrets.test.tsx.

features.rationale: Requires a pending request in the fixture; approval is a single PUT with visible state, mutating only the throwaway home — no external account.

features.title: Open a job's detail drawer and read its logs
features.user_story: As a user, I want to inspect a job's last result and logs, so that I can debug a failing schedule.
features.entry_path: /schedule → click job row → drawer → Logs tab

preconditions.notes: Drawer tabs 'details' and 'logs' at SchedulePage.tsx ~L1491.

features.rationale: Needs jobs with execution history; web-only.

features.title: Monitor loops
features.user_story: As a user, I want same-session bounded monitors and nudge loops I can arm, inspect and stop from the composer popover, so that the agent babysits something for me.
features.entry_path: Chat composer → monitor popover; Crew Members → Crew summary → Auto patrol (read-only)

preconditions.notes: Seed one active monitor via POST /api/monitors so the popover shows a cycle readout.

features.rationale: Popover state is fixture-seedable via the local API; the loop firing itself is timing-based and not asserted.

features.title: Template update signal

features.entry_path: Schedule → job detail (TemplateUpdatedNotice)

features.rationale: Purely fixture-driven notice; deterministic render and dismiss.

features.title: Agent chat egress

features.rationale: No UI and requires a live provider; not pixel-testable.

features.title: Settings › Webhooks

features.title: Webhooks (full page)

features.title: Settings › Channels

features.title: Channels: create a multi-agent channel from a preset and post a message
features.user_story: As a lead, I want to create a channel from a team preset with role-assigned agents and post an @mention, so that several agents collaborate in one readable transcript.

features.entry_path: Settings > Chat > Restore Sessions toggle > Restore Window select

preconditions.notes: Restore Window select is dependent on Restore Sessions being on.

features.rationale: Effect requires reload; still web-testable via page reload in Playwright.

features.title: Toggle feature previews (Crew Members, Chat on a crew, Webhooks)
features.user_story: As an early adopter, I want to turn on a feature preview in Settings > Developer, so that unfinished surfaces appear in the dashboard.
features.entry_path: Settings > Developer > Feature Previews > toggle Crew Members / Chat on a crew / Webhooks

preconditions.notes: Per-device flags; Webhooks flag reveals the Settings > Webhooks tab without reload.

features.rationale: Client-side flags with observable nav changes.

features.title: Change dashboard Language
features.user_story: As a non-English user, I want to change the dashboard Language in Settings > Display, so that the UI is shown in my language.
features.entry_path: Settings > Display > Language select

preconditions.notes: Tab rail labels are rebuilt per render (buildTabs) so they must re-translate without reload. | Chromium launched with --lang=en-US, so Auto resolves to English; an explicit choice writes dashboard.language.

features.rationale: I18n switch is client-side; assert rail labels change language.

features.title: Configure sidebar session colours (palette, default, display mode, intensity)
features.user_story: As a dashboard user, I want to set the session colour palette and defaults in Settings > Display, so that sidebar rows are colour-coded.
features.entry_path: Settings > Display > Session colours: Palette, Default for New Sessions, Display Mode, Intensity

preconditions.notes: Also Highlight recent sessions stepper.

features.rationale: Multi-control visual configuration verifiable against sidebar rows.

features.title: Configure built-in terminal (shell, font, size, completion)
features.user_story: As a developer, I want to set the terminal shell, font, font size and command completion in Settings > Display, so that the built-in terminal matches my workflow.
features.entry_path: Settings > Display > Terminal section

preconditions.notes: configKeys dashboard.terminal.shell and dashboard.terminal.completion.enabled; terminal availability depends on terminalRegistry.

features.rationale: Persistence is web-testable; launching the terminal to observe the shell is environment dependent.

features.title: Adjust Zoom Level
features.user_story: As a dashboard user, I want to step the Zoom Level in Settings > Display, so that the UI is larger or smaller.
features.entry_path: Settings > Display > Zoom Level stepper

preconditions.notes: In Electron zoom is applied via webFrame; in web it may be CSS-based.

features.rationale: Stepper is web-renderable; note the zoom effect may differ between Electron and browser.

features.title: Import agent configuration from other tools
features.user_story: As a new user, I want to import existing agent setups, so that I do not start from scratch.
features.entry_path: Settings > Imports > start import (fires mc-start-import to reopen AgentImportFlow)

preconditions.notes: ImportPanel.tsx; same flow as onboarding chapter 1. | Also hosts the Back up / restore configuration (PortabilityTab) section.

features.rationale: Reads local tool config paths; safe in fixture; web-only.

features.title: Override sound per notification category
features.user_story: As a dashboard user, I want to choose a different sound for Approval or Cron notifications, so that I can tell them apart by ear.
features.entry_path: Settings > Notifications > category selects (Agent replies, Approval, Cron, Subagent, Tasks, Webhook, Skills, Heartbeat)

preconditions.notes: Each select offers Default plus presets none/chime/ding/blip/pop/pulse.

features.rationale: Select persistence testable; preview playback is not observable.

features.title: Toggle Play sound on new notifications and set volume
features.user_story: As a dashboard user, I want to toggle notification sounds and adjust Volume, so that alerts are audible at my preferred level.
features.entry_path: Settings > Notifications > Play sound on new notifications toggle > Volume stepper

preconditions.notes: Settings stored via loadSoundSettings/saveSoundSettings (localStorage).

features.rationale: Persistence and dependent-control enablement are testable; audio playback is not.

features.title: Mute a notification source or override its priority
features.user_story: As a dashboard user, I want to mute a noisy notification source in Settings > Notifications > Sources, so that it stops badging and sounding.
features.entry_path: Settings > Notifications > Sources list > mute toggle / priority select per source

preconditions.notes: Sources come from the backend notification channel registry.

features.rationale: Requires backend-provided source list; fake backend can supply it.

features.title: Toggle Send anonymous usage heartbeat
features.user_story: As a user, I want to opt in or out of the anonymous usage heartbeat, so that I decide whether a beacon is sent on launch.
features.entry_path: Settings > Privacy > Send anonymous usage heartbeat toggle

preconditions.notes: configKey telemetry.beacon_enabled; 'Saved for future launches'.

features.rationale: Simple config toggle with persistence assertion.

features.title: Settings › Releases
features.user_story: As a user, I want a release channel, update check and changelog, so that I stay current on my terms.
features.entry_path: Settings → Releases

preconditions.notes: Update check hits the network; stub it. Do not apply an update. | Fixed-height contained tab; rows come from CHANGELOG.md sections plus the running build. | updateAffordance decides apply vs command; About also hosts Support/ReportProblemCard and MobileLoginCard.

features.rationale: Changelog and channel selector render offline; applying an update is excluded.

features.title: Toggle Use Ctrl (not Option) for chat 1-9
features.user_story: As a Mac user, I want chat-tab switching bound to Ctrl+digit instead of Option+digit, so that it does not conflict with typing special characters.
features.entry_path: Settings > Shortcuts > Use Ctrl (not Option) for chat 1-9 toggle

preconditions.notes: Verify by pressing the new chord and asserting tab switch.

features.rationale: Web-testable keyboard behaviour with multiple open sessions.

features.title: Change Search Everywhere activation shortcut (preset or custom chord)
features.user_story: As a keyboard user, I want to pick double-Shift, Cmd/Ctrl+K or record a custom chord for Search Everywhere, so that the palette opens with my preferred keys.
features.entry_path: Settings > Shortcuts > Search Everywhere button group > custom > Record > press chord

preconditions.notes: Custom mode enters recording without persisting until a valid chord is captured; Escape cancels.

features.rationale: Keyboard recording is testable with Playwright keypresses in Chromium.

features.title: Toggle Auto-speak Responses
features.user_story: As a dashboard user, I want to enable Auto-speak Responses, so that every assistant reply is read aloud.
features.entry_path: Settings > Voice > Auto-speak Responses toggle

preconditions.notes: Audio output is not observable headlessly.

features.rationale: Persistence-only assertion; speech output cannot be pixel-verified.

features.title: View Voice panel (TTS + speech-to-text)
features.user_story: As a dashboard user, I want to open Settings > Voice, so that I can configure spoken replies and dictation.
features.entry_path: Settings > Preferences > Voice

preconditions.notes: VoicePanel renders TTS provider cards and embeds SttSettings.

features.rationale: Render-only check; audio devices are absent in Xvfb so assertions stop at UI.

features.title: Configure push-to-talk shortcut key and mode
features.user_story: As a dashboard user, I want to set the dictation Shortcut key and how it works (hold/tap/both), so that I can start recording from the keyboard.
features.entry_path: Settings > Voice > Speech to text > Shortcut key select, How the key works button group, Tap vs hold cutoff

preconditions.notes: Platform copy differs Mac vs other.

features.rationale: Control rendering and persistence are web-testable.

features.title: Enable speech-to-text and pick provider
features.user_story: As a dashboard user, I want to enable dictation and choose Local or Transcribe in Settings > Voice, so that I can speak into the message box.
features.entry_path: Settings > Voice > Speech to text card > Enabled toggle > Provider select

preconditions.notes: Transcribe requires AWS credentials; local requires model download.

features.rationale: UI state changes are testable; Transcribe end-to-end is needs-secret and microphone capture is not available headlessly.

features.title: Switch TTS Provider (built-in / Piper / Amazon Polly)
features.user_story: As a dashboard user, I want to switch the TTS Provider in Settings > Voice, so that spoken replies use the engine I choose.
features.entry_path: Settings > Voice > Provider select (TTS card)

preconditions.notes: Selecting Polly reveals AWS profile/region inputs; Piper reveals binary/model paths.

features.rationale: Conditional field rendering is web-testable; actual synthesis for Polly would be needs-secret.

features.title: Check for updates and install
features.user_story: As a desktop user, I want to click Check for updates in Settings > About and install one, so that I am on the latest build.
features.entry_path: Settings > About > Check for updates > Install and restart

preconditions.notes: Hits the real release feed and restarts the app.

features.rationale: Network-dependent and restarts the application; not pixel-testable.

features.title: Install playwright-cli and a browser engine from Settings
features.user_story: As a dashboard user, I want to click Install in Settings > Browser and pick an engine, so that browsing becomes available without a terminal.
features.entry_path: Settings > Browser > Install > choose engine (chromium/firefox/webkit) > watch steps npm/browser/skills

preconditions.notes: Runs npm install and downloads a browser; writes to the host.

features.rationale: Network download and host mutation; not pixel-testable deterministically.

features.title: Toggle Prevent sleep while running
features.user_story: As a desktop user, I want to enable Prevent sleep while running, so that my machine stays awake during long tasks.
features.entry_path: Settings > Chat > Prevent sleep while running toggle

preconditions.notes: configKey dashboard.prevent_sleep; the power-save blocker only exists in Electron.

features.rationale: Toggle persistence is web-testable (degradable), but the actual sleep-inhibit effect needs Electron.

features.title: Toggle Run a local gateway
features.user_story: As a desktop user, I want to turn off the local gateway, so that the app acts as a client to a remote gateway on next launch.
features.entry_path: Settings > Developer > Gateway > Run a local gateway toggle

preconditions.notes: Section only renders when the Electron bridge is present; takes effect on next app open.

features.rationale: Desktop-app-only section; not degradable to web because it is hidden without Electron.

features.title: Toggle Notify when a background chat finishes
features.user_story: As a multitasking user, I want a system notification when a background chat finishes while the window is hidden, so that I can return to it.
features.entry_path: Settings > Notifications > Notify when a background chat finishes toggle

preconditions.notes: System notifications only fire while window is minimized/behind another app.

features.rationale: Toggle persistence is web-testable (degradable), but OS notification delivery needs Electron and window focus state.

features.title: UI preference host backup
features.user_story: As a user whose dashboard port or Electron userData moved, I want my browser-held settings restored from the host, so that I do not reconfigure everything.
features.entry_path: No panel; lib/uiPrefs.ts syncs allowlisted keys via /api/ui-prefs

preconditions.notes: Only DURABLE_PREF_KEYS are backed up; mc-yolo-ack is excluded.

features.rationale: Cross-cutting mechanism with no UI of its own; verified through the settings rows it backs, not pixels.

features.title: Download a local STT model
features.user_story: As a dashboard user, I want to select a local speech model and click Download now, so that dictation works offline.
features.entry_path: Settings > Voice > Speech to text > Model select > Download now

preconditions.notes: Downloads a large model from the network.

features.rationale: Requires large external download and disk writes; not suitable for pixel tests.

features.title: Install a Level-0 colour pack from a local directory and select it
features.user_story: As a user, I want to install a theme pack from a folder on disk, so that it appears in the single Theme dropdown.
features.entry_path: Settings > Display > Install theme > local path

preconditions.notes: Harness pre-writes a minimal theme.json (formatVersion 1, level 0, variables) under $KIROCREW_SCRATCH; path is typed. Watch for the 'Applying…' indicator.

features.rationale: Local install path spawns nothing and needs no network; validation and promotion are on-host.

features.title: Selecting an installed L2 pack with a persona shows the consent modal verbatim before first chat
features.user_story: As a user, I want to see exactly the persona text a theme will inject and consent to it, so that nothing surprising reaches the agent.
features.entry_path: Settings > Display > select installed L2 pack > Chat > first message

preconditions.notes: Harness writes an L2 pack with persona.md locally first; consent hash lives in localStorage and a reinstall with changed text re-prompts.

features.rationale: All local: install, modal, hash-gated injection on the canned fake turn; the modal and re-prompt are visible.

features.title: Install a theme pack from a github.com URL
features.user_story: As a user, I want to paste a GitHub repo URL, so that the pack is cloned and installed.
features.entry_path: Settings > Display > Install theme > GitHub URL

preconditions.notes: Server-side shallow clone through the sandbox chokepoint; fails closed with 503 where no sandbox backend exists.

features.rationale: Needs outbound network to github.com (and a sandbox backend), unavailable on the target.

features.title: Settings › Security
features.user_story: As an owner, I want denied commands, sensitive paths and the approval posture in one place, so that I can tighten what agents may do.
features.entry_path: Settings > Security > section rail > /settings/security/<section> (posture default, approval, rules, tailnet, apps, layers, governance, docs)

preconditions.notes: Add and remove one user rule; file-delivery consent has no panel yet. | SECURITY_SECTIONS in SecurityPanel.tsx; approval mode also cycled by keyboard shortcut in App.tsx. | Rendered from GET /api/security/posture registry via PostureDisclosureRow.

features.rationale: Core operator surface; section switching is fast and visually distinct, and the default Posture section renders read-only from a stubbable /api/security/posture. Rule CRUD is its own nightly record.

features.title: Settings › Secrets
features.user_story: As a user, I want managed integration credentials and other vault entries, so that secrets live encrypted, not in config.
features.entry_path: Settings → Secrets

preconditions.notes: Use a placeholder secret name/value; delete it afterwards. | SecretsPanel.tsx; values masked by default. | Non-2xx responses keep the form populated; unused-reason hints for WakaTime/Jira.

features.rationale: Add/list/delete a placeholder entry needs no real credential.

features.title: Set how long auto-approve stays on
features.user_story: As a user, I want to choose the auto-approve duration in Settings > Security > Approval, so that YOLO mode expires when I expect.
features.entry_path: Settings > Security > Approval > How long auto-approve stays on button group

preconditions.notes: configKey agent.yolo_duration; rail shows expiry summary.

features.rationale: Button group persistence and rail summary update are web-testable.

features.title: View Security docs/reference section
features.user_story: As an operator, I want to open Settings > Security > Docs, so that I can find links to the security documentation.
features.entry_path: Settings > Security > Docs

preconditions.notes: External links open in a new tab.

features.rationale: Static reference content.

features.title: View Governance Policy section
features.user_story: As a governed user, I want to see the active governance policy and its scopes (access, io, channels, modes), so that I know which controls an admin has set.
features.entry_path: Settings > Security > Governance > Governance Policy

preconditions.notes: Reads governance distribution/policy endpoints; standard OSS build shows all-permitted.

features.rationale: Read-only render from stubbable governance endpoints.

features.title: View Defense-in-depth Layers section
features.user_story: As an operator, I want to read the enforced security layers list, so that I understand what protections apply.
features.entry_path: Settings > Security > Layers

preconditions.notes: Static FEATURES registry with translated labels.

features.rationale: Static content; good for i18n/pixel regression.

features.title: Create a mobile login link
features.user_story: As a user, I want to generate a one-time mobile login link from Settings > Security, so that I can sign in on my phone.
features.entry_path: Settings > Security > MobileLoginCard > Create link > Copy

preconditions.notes: Sends the active slot's session key; refused in incognito/temporary sessions.

features.rationale: Mints a short-lived credential via API; testable with a stub but avoid asserting on the token value.

features.title: Add and remove a custom denied-command pattern
features.user_story: As an operator, I want to add a regex to Your custom denies in Settings > Security > Rules and remove it again, so that the PreToolUse gate blocks commands I choose.
features.entry_path: Settings > Security > Rules > Denied Commands > Your custom denies > Add > Trash

preconditions.notes: Draft is lifted to the panel so switching sections does not lose it; built-in rules are read-only.

features.rationale: CRUD on user rules via API with visible table update; built-in list unaffected.

features.title: Configure tailnet access in Security
features.user_story: As an operator, I want to expose the dashboard over my tailnet, so that I can reach it from other devices.
features.entry_path: Settings > Security > Tailnet section

preconditions.notes: Covered by SecurityPanel.tailnet.test.tsx; TailnetMobileCard on Overview. | Requires tailnet status from backend; disabled when no tailnet detected.

features.rationale: Re-tiered needs-secret -> nightly: the fake backend stubs tailnet status, so the section and the Trust-this-machine toggle render and persist offline. A real Tailscale daemon/account is not required for the UI assertion (toggle is disabled when no tailnet is detected, which is also a valid stubbed state).

features.title: Toggle Trust every third-party app
features.user_story: As an operator, I want to decide whether third-party apps run their own code without asking, so that I balance convenience against safety.
features.entry_path: Settings > Security > Apps > Trust every third-party app toggle

preconditions.notes: Off by default; per-app trust rows listed below.

features.rationale: Security-relevant toggle; testable against stubbed trusted-apps data.

features.title: Developer › Agent backend
features.user_story: As a developer, I want to see which agent harness backend is live and whether Kiro prerequisites are met, so that I know what turns run on.
features.entry_path: Developer → agent-backend tab (?tab=agent-backend)

preconditions.notes: Shows the fake ACP backend in the nightly harness. READ-ONLY: do not click the backend switch — changing the binding restarts sessions and detaches the harness's fake ACP backend.

features.rationale: Read-only status view is a useful harness confidence check (asserts the fake backend is what is live). one reader marked the record excluded because switching backends breaks the harness; that action is scoped out here rather than dropping the view, so the tier is nightly.

features.title: Developer › Archive
features.user_story: As a developer, I want a consolidated session archive browser, so that I can inspect compacted history.
features.entry_path: Developer → archive tab (?tab=archive)

preconditions.notes: Fixture includes at least one archive file.

features.rationale: Read-only list and detail from fixture archives.

features.title: Developer › Config
features.user_story: As a developer, I want raw Kiro Crew and agent config editors, so that I can fix a setting no panel exposes.
features.entry_path: Developer → config tab (?tab=config)

preconditions.notes: Edit a harmless key and revert.

features.rationale: Editor round-trip through the config API is deterministic and reversible.

features.title: Developer › Debug tools
features.user_story: As a developer, I want diagnostic overlays such as the chat scroll inspector, so that I can debug layout issues.
features.entry_path: Developer → debug-tools tab (?tab=debug-tools)
features.rationale: Client-only overlay toggle; visible in a chat afterwards.

features.title: Developer › Logs
features.user_story: As a developer, I want a live gateway log stream with level control, so that I can debug in real time.
features.entry_path: Developer → logs tab (?tab=logs)
features.rationale: Stream renders lines from the running gateway; level POST is reversible.

features.title: Developer › MCP pool
features.user_story: As a developer, I want MCP connection pool state and a probe, so that I can diagnose tool outages.
features.entry_path: Developer → mcp-pool tab (?tab=mcp-pool)
features.rationale: Active/scopes render from the connections fixture; probe is a local call.

features.title: Memory graph
features.user_story: As a developer, I want an entity/relation visualiser over the memory store plus every memory layer and saved lesson, so that I can debug and audit what the agent remembers.
features.entry_path: Developer → memory tab (?tab=memory)

preconditions.notes: Canvas graph; assert node count rather than layout. Vector stores are absent by design; only markdown layers (preferences, projects, semantic, history) and three lessons in lessons.jsonl are seeded.

features.rationale: Developer-mode internals view; graph layout is non-deterministic so assertions stay coarse, but the layer text and lesson rows are deterministic local reads.

features.title: Navigate the Developer page internals tabs
features.user_story: As a developer, I want logs, system, telemetry, storage, MCP pool, memory graph, config, agent backend, debug tools, and archive in one place, so that I can diagnose the gateway.
features.entry_path: Enable dev mode → Rail bottom → Developer → tabs (logs, system, telemetry, storage, mcp-pool, memory, config, agent-backend, debug-tools, archive)

preconditions.notes: Rail row only with mc-dev-mode=1 but route always resolves; MemoryGraphTab lazy; /logs also standalone.

features.rationale: Tab-tour flow (every tab mounts without error) distinct from the per-tab inspection records below; several tabs depend on backend probes; web-only.

features.title: Developer › Storage
features.user_story: As a developer, I want a raw localStorage inspector, so that I can debug client preferences.
features.entry_path: Developer → storage tab (?tab=storage)
features.rationale: Client-only table; deterministic once localStorage is seeded.

features.title: Developer › System
features.user_story: As a developer, I want host runtime, services, sessions and performance views, so that I can spot resource problems and reclaim session storage.
features.entry_path: Developer → system tab (?tab=system) → sub-tabs Sessions | Services | Performance → SessionStorageScreen

preconditions.notes: Numbers vary; assert structure not values. pages/system/*; HostRuntimeCard shows host info. Deletion actions exist but only read-only inspection is exercised.

features.rationale: Read-only; metric values are non-deterministic so assertions stay structural. Seed sessions-long-history so the storage screen has rows.

features.title: Developer › Telemetry
features.user_story: As a developer, I want startup timings and context traces, so that I can find slow paths.
features.entry_path: Developer → telemetry tab (?tab=telemetry)
features.rationale: Read-only tables from the running process.

features.title: Logs (full page)
features.user_story: As an operator, I want a full-page log viewer, so that I can watch the gateway without dashboard chrome distraction.
features.entry_path: Type /logs
features.rationale: Same viewer as the Developer tab at a stable URL; distinct route so kept separate from developer-logs.
